title: FHIR R4 vs purpose-built REST for year one
subtitle: Custom JSON for RapidChart and CensusBoard; mapping layer only if a payer or HIE demands it
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Priya Nair (EM), Rahul Deshmukh (PM), backend engineers, Riverview architecture review
owners: Aman Kumar (design), Kavya Menon (ChartLine adapters), Rahul Deshmukh (vendor pressure)
related: RVH-PRD-2020-019, RVH-PRD-2021-006 (later assemble PRD), ChartLine vendor notes 2020-09-22, spike RVH-1744
summary: Decision record for the first year of Riverview patient-api: we will not speak FHIR R4 as the primary contract. RapidChart and CensusBoard are two Java apps that want small, stable JSON. ChartLine cannot emit FHIR. The team is five people, none of us a FHIR specialist. Vendors will keep pushing R4. We will ship a purpose-built REST assemble and read API, and we will keep a door open for a mapping layer if a payer or HIE writes it into a contract. This document is the trade-off, the edges that would smash our payload budget (contained resources, Patient $everything), and the alternative we killed after spike RVH-1744.
form_description: Technical design choosing custom REST over FHIR R4 for Riverview patient-api v1, with constraints, payload math, and a rejected HAPI-on-day-one path.

blocks.text: Decision

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: v1 of patient-api is purpose-built REST (JSON over HTTPS, our schemas, our error model). We do not expose FHIR R4 resources as the contract RapidChart and CensusBoard consume. We do not stand up HAPI FHIR as the system of record. If a payer, HIE, or state reporting feed later requires FHIR, we add a mapping service in front of the same assemble internals. ChartLine stays on its XML/JSON interface. We will not wait for ChartLine to grow a FHIR endpoint; their TAM said 2022 'maybe' on September 22, which is not a date.

Priya signed this on October 6 with the staffing note: five people on the account through mid-2021 (Priya, Rahul, Aman, Kavya, Sneha; Luis Ortega joining in November for LDAP/identity, not FHIR). No FHIR specialist hire. Chris Patel can measure feeds; he is not writing StructureDefinitions. Diego Alvarez is not on this account yet. Dr. Anita Shah's ask from the CMIO office is a safer chart assemble for RapidChart, not a strategic FHIR platform. Denise Howell was not in the architecture review; nursing did not request R4.
Why this is even a question

Two vendor meetings in September (ChartLine workshop Sep 22, a payer IT intro Sep 29) used the same slide: 'FHIR R4, US Core, 2021.' Rahul needed an engineering answer that was not 'we will look into it.' RapidChart's app lead Gita Raman sent a one-pager on September 18 titled What we actually HTTP GET, which is four endpoints and a 50 KB JSON budget. CensusBoard's Omar Haddad wants a census row, not a Bundle. If we give them FHIR because a vendor room clapped, we will spend the year teaching Java teams to parse Bundles while ChartLine still hands us non-FHIR XML.

Spike RVH-1744 (Kavya + Aman, Sep 28-Oct 1) ran HAPI FHIR 5.1.0 in stage against a fake Patient + AllergyIntolerance set derived from ChartLine fixtures. We did not connect prod ChartLine. Numbers below are from that spike, 1000 synthetic patients, last 5 encounters stuffed as contained Encounter resources because that is what every 'just use $everything' blog post does.

blocks.text: Consumers and what they want

Internal consumers for v1 are only those two Java apps. Nursing informatics (Denise) talks to RapidChart, not to our OpenAPI. Anita talks to Denise and to us. A future HIE would be a third consumer with a different SLA and a different legal wrapper. We will not design v1 as if the HIE is already in the room. That is how you ship a mediocre API for everyone.

This is enough to argue the shape against FHIR. Detailed assemble fields live in the product requirements (RVH-PRD-2020-019 now; a tighter assemble PRD will follow when nursing timings land). IDs are our merge keys, not FHIR ids.

blocks.text: What FHIR R4 would have meant on the hot path

If RapidChart called GET /Patient/{id}/$everything, HAPI in our spike returned a Bundle with Patient, AllergyIntolerance x N, MedicationStatement x N, Encounter x 5, Condition x N, plus search metadata. For fixture PEDS-heavy allergy lists (14.2 allergies mean on the peds fixture, not typical med-surg), encoded JSON was 172-248 KB. RapidChart's 120 KB warn fired. Contained Encounter.location.managingOrganization.contained... we stopped counting. Contained resources are legal FHIR and a gift for people who want one HTTP round trip. They are how you smash a 50 KB p95 budget without noticing in a demo.

$everything is the worst case, but even GET /AllergyIntolerance?patient=X as a separate resource type means RapidChart makes 5-7 HTTP calls where they currently want 1. Their app servers are not a browser. Gita's one-pager said one round trip for the opening chart view. FHIR's resource-oriented purity fights that. A FHIR _revinclude assemble is just us inventing a Bundle-shaped assemble anyway, with worse tooling for our team.

blocks.text: Other FHIR edges that bit the spike

items: AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus vs verificationStatus vs our ChartLine 'active/inactive/error' triad. We spent 6.5 hours arguing mapping for one vendor field. Nursing will not wait for that per field across meds and problems.
Contained resources: once you contain, clients must walk graph edges. RapidChart will write bugs. We will debug graphs at 3am. No.

Patient.$everything would include notes if we were honest, and notes are SiteNotes, flaky, large. Out of scope for assemble even in REST (text search explicitly later). FHIR makes it tempting to 'include DocumentReference' because the operation exists.
IDs: FHIR wants stable Patient.id. Our merge keys will move when identity merge ships. We would mint FHIR ids that then split or collide. That is a support nightmare for an HIE we do not have yet.
SMART scopes: we have LDAP groups. Mapping groups to patient/*.read is a year of IAM, not a library import.

blocks.text: Trade-offs (honest)

Custom REST is not free. We own versioning. We will be asked 'why not FHIR' in every vendor meeting until a mapping layer exists. New engineers will grep for Patient and find none. Sneha has to maintain our JSON schemas instead of downloading US Core. If Riverview signs an HIE contract in 2021, we will look late. That is a business risk Rahul is accepting in writing at the end of this doc.

FHIR as v1 is not free either. We would still map ChartLine. We would still not have SMART. We would still blow RapidChart's budget on peds. We would spend Sneha on validator noise (the spike produced 40+ warning-level issues per patient, many from missing US Core Must Support fields ChartLine never had). We would hire or fake a FHIR specialist. Priya does not have budget. The 'interop win' would be a facade.

blocks.text: If the payer wants FHIR, they can put it in the contract and we will staff a mapper. Do not spend the allergy screen on a Bundle.
Rejected alternative: HAPI in front, REST a private impl

The attractive compromise from the Sep 22 workshop: expose FHIR publicly, keep internal assemble, translate at the edge. We rejected it for year one. Two public contracts means two test surfaces for Sneha, two auth stories, and someone (usually on-call) has to know which face is broken. RapidChart would be told to 'just use FHIR' by someone in a vendor meeting, then Gita would page us because Bundle.entry[3].resource.contained is null. A mapping layer later, behind a flag, for a named consumer, is different: one extra deploy, not the default path for the floor.

A second rejected idea: FHIR only for Patient and Encounter, custom for allergies. That split is how you teach the worst of both. Killed in the Oct 2 working session. One assemble JSON for the opening view.
Mapping layer later (door, not a project)

If a payer or HIE demands R4, proposed shape (not staffed): a separate deploy fhir-map in namespace riverview-chart, read-only, calling the same internal assemble service patient-api-int:8080, emitting a small set of resources (Patient, AllergyIntolerance, MedicationStatement, Encounter, Condition). No $everything. No contained. No US Core validation on the hot path; batch validate in CI against fixtures. SMART out of scope until Jordan Hale has a timeline. This paragraph is permission to start a TDD later, not permission to open a /fhir route in 1.0.

Triggers that would reopen this TDD: signed contract naming FHIR R4; ChartLine ships a real FHIR endpoint we can probe; Riverview hires a FHIR specialist onto this account. Tweets and webinars are not triggers. Rahul owns saying no in vendor rooms. Aman owns saying no in code reviews that add hapi as a dependency 'just to try.'

blocks.text: Anita's comment in the review, paraphrased with her ok: the CMIO office is tired of interface projects that optimize for the next conference. She will support a mapping layer when a counterparty is real. Until then she wants allergies and a chart that does not lie when SiteNotes is down. That is REST we control.
Failure modes if we pick REST and then half-implement FHIR anyway

This section exists because the spike branch still has a package org.northstar.rvh.fhir.scratch that someone will try to merge 'so we do not lose the work.' Kavya will delete it on October 9. If it comes back, treat it as a product change, not a cleanup.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: Do not add a hidden /fhir/Patient route behind an Accept header. RapidChart's RestTemplate will send */* and you will accidentally serve Bundles to the floor. If you need a mapper later, it is a different host name, different deploy, different auth allowlist.

ChartLine XML for allergies on fixture MEDSURG-A is 6.1 KB. Our JSON block is 2.4 KB. The HAPI AllergyIntolerance for the same row was 4.8 KB each because of meta.profile, text.div narrative we did not ask for, and a CodeableConcept with three coding entries (SNOMED, a ChartLine local code, and a leftover ICD string that was not an allergy code). Multiply by 14.2 mean allergies on the peds fixture and you have already spent the RapidChart budget on narrative HTML. HAPI generates text.div by default. Turning it off is a flag nobody will remember in a hotfix.

Identity is the other smash. We do not have a stable Patient.id. The current lookup key is ChartLine MRN plus facility, hashed into merge_key mk_<12 hex> which will change when RVH-TDD-2021-004 lands. If we had minted FHIR ids in October 2020, HIM would own a crosswalk table by March, and every HIE subscriber would cache the old id. Custom REST lets us call it patient_id and document that it is not durable yet. That sentence is awkward and is also true. FHIR would make the same awkwardness look like a spec violation.
Worked payload math (so this is not vibes)

RapidChart's 50 KB p95 target is for the whole assemble body, gzip off, because their Java parser reads the entity before gzip stats matter on the workstation. Gzip helps the wire, not Gita's 50 KB warn. Numbers from spike fixture MEDSURG-A (62-year-old, 3 allergies, 8 active meds, 5 encounters, 6 problems) and PEDS-ALLERGY (6-year-old, 14 allergies, 4 meds, 5 encounters, 2 problems).

blocks.text: BH-SHORT is the case vendors use in demos ('FHIR is fine, look how small'). It is not MAIN ED at 16:00. If a future mapper ships, it should cap AllergyIntolerance count, strip text.div, and refuse $everything. Those rules are easier to enforce on a dedicated deploy than on the RapidChart hot path.
ChartLine adapter notes (why passthrough was never real)

The interface at chartline-iface-prod.rvh.internal:8443 (stage: chartline-iface-stage.rvh.internal:8443) speaks a vendor JSON twin that looks 'modern' in a slide and is not R4. Allergy rows use fields AllergenName, SeverityCode, StatusCd, OnsetText. There is no system|code pair. Medication rows use OrderName, DoseFreeText, FreqCode. Encounter rows use EncNbr, AdmitDtm, EncTypeCd. Kavya's adapter maps those to our block objects. A FHIR mapper would map the same fields a second time into CodeableConcepts with dummy systems like http://rvh.internal/chartline/allergen, which is not US Core and would fail any partner's validator. We would then get a project to 'clean the codes' that is actually a terminology service. Five people. No.

SiteNotes is HTTP POST /fetchNotes with a facility+MRN body, 14.6s timeout on their side, our client timeout 800ms if we ever call it from assemble, which v1 will not. Friday 16:00-18:30 Eastern their index job holds locks. That is a REST banner problem. In FHIR it becomes a DocumentReference search timeout that $everything would drag into the opening view. Out of scope here except as a warning: do not 'include notes because FHIR has the type.'
Auth and versioning under REST

v1 auth is hospital LDAP via bearer tokens RapidChart already has. We introspect group membership. SMART on FHIR would want launch context, scopes, and a different token. Jordan Hale said October 5 that SMART is 'on a list' behind two other IAM projects. Building SMART as a side effect of picking R4 is how we miss the RapidChart date. Custom REST lets us keep LDAP and document it.

Versioning: URL prefix /v1/. Breaking field changes go to /v2/. Additive fields on assemble blocks are allowed in v1 if Sneha's tests permit unknown properties on the RapidChart side (Gita said they ignore extras as of 4.2.0). We will not use FHIR's meta.versionId as a substitute for API versioning. We will not put the word R4 in the URL to satisfy a procurement checklist.

blocks.text: How to say no in a vendor room (Rahul's language)

Rahul asked for a paragraph he can read out. Here: Northstar is building a purpose-built REST assemble for RapidChart and CensusBoard in 2020-2021 because ChartLine does not emit FHIR, the consumers want small JSON, and the team does not include a FHIR specialist. If a payer or HIE contract requires R4, we will staff a mapping service against the same internals. We are not committing to US Core, SMART, or $everything on this account this fiscal year. Point them at this doc id RVH-TDD-2020-011. If they need a date, the honest one is 'after a signed requirement,' not Q2.

Sneha's test strategy (RVH-QA-2021-007 will exist later) should assert JSON Schema for /v1/chart/assemble, not a FHIR validator. If someone adds a CI job hapifhir/validator, fail the PR that added it unless the mapping deploy is in the same PR with a named consumer. Priya will back that rule.

Luis Ortega starts in November. His first identity work should not include FHIR Patient identifiers. Chris Patel may store assemble timings in the ops warehouse; he may not store assemble bodies. Denise and Anita do not need to re-approve this TDD unless the protocol changes. End of design.
